Definition: from G393; a rising of light, i.e. dawn (figuratively); by implication, the east (also in plural):--dayspring, east, rising.
BiblicalUsage: Anatole is the rising, the dawn and the east where the sun comes up. The wise men come from the east following His star, Zechariah sings that the dayspring from on high has visited us, and Jesus says His coming will be like lightning shining from the east to the west. The word joins the direction of sunrise to the hope of a new day.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God tied His promises to the sunrise on purpose: every morning rehearses the coming of the Light. The dayspring has already visited us in Christ, and I hold that His return will be just as unmistakable as the dawn.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Zechariah, Father of John the Baptist
RelatedEvents: The Magi Visit Jesus; The Annunciation to Mary
